text.arabic_uthmani: مِن فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ

words.gloss_range: preposition marking source, origin, and separation in continuation from the prior rescue clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: named governed source from which rescue is completed
later classifying prepositional phrase that reverses the opening source relation

words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) opens 44:31 by completing the rescue grammar carried over from 44:30: Pharaoh is first the source and enclosing domain from which deliverance occurred, not yet the subject of a fresh sentence. That source sense also carries separation, so the phrase makes rescue feel like removal from an oppressive regime. The repeated particle shape later returns in {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}), where the relation changes from Israel being brought away from Pharaoh to Pharaoh being placed inside a class of excess. Even the small opening particle is not weightless: its m-n nasal contour binds audibly into the heavy governed name {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}). A variant reading can expose the pressure point by turning the opening into a question, but the canonical local grammar keeps {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) as the preposition governing {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}).

topics.headline: rescue source completed after the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 44:31 begins inside the unfinished rescue construction from 44:30, so Pharaoh is first framed as the oppressive source escaped from.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) as the preposition governing {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}), continuing the prior rescue-source phrase from 44:30.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that changing the particle would move Pharaoh from governed source to questioned nominative, which clarifies what the canonical preposition is doing.
topics.reason: The variant {{ar:مَنْ فِرْعَوْنُ}} ({{tr:man firʿawnu}}) is useful as contrast, but the aligned canonical word is {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) with genitive governance.

topics.headline: same particle shape reverses relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same particle form first marks escape from Pharaoh and then Pharaoh's placement among excessives.
topics.reason: The ayah contains the opening {{ar:مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:min firʿawna}}) and the closing {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}), with different local relations.

topics.headline: small particle binds to the heavy name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the light opening particle attach sonically to the heavy ruler-name it governs.
topics.reason: The row is anchored in the local sequence {{ar:مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:min firʿawna}}), so its sound observation has a concrete grammatical base.

words.gloss_range: foreign proper name and ruler-title functioning as governed rescue-source and antecedent for the following pronoun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the name as source of rescue
following pronoun bundle that resumes the name

words.prose: {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) is not a free-standing dramatic name here; it is genitive under {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}), so Pharaoh first appears as the source from which rescue had to happen. A nominative variant would make the name the answerable term in a question, but the canonical wording keeps it governed as escape-source. The same name then becomes the antecedent of the pronoun in {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}), letting the ayah move from named source to pronominal diagnosis without changing subjects. Because the name functions as both individual and regime-title, deliverance is from the person and the order concentrated in him. Its dense f-r-ʿ-w-n sound profile gives the foreign ruler-title weight before the lighter particle-and-copula diagnosis begins. The wider Pharaoh pattern matters: his claim to highest status (79:24), his political elevation in the land (28:4), and the height-excess pairing (10:83) all converge when 44:31 reduces the name to a judged case of overbearing excess.

topics.headline: Pharaoh is first the escaped source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Pharaoh is introduced by grammar as the source of deliverance before he is morally described.
topics.reason: QAC parses {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) as the genitive object of {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}).

topics.headline: variant nominative shows what canonical governance prevents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that a nominative variant would make Pharaoh the answerable term of a question, while the canonical wording keeps him governed as escape-source.
topics.reason: The variant {{ar:مَنْ فِرْعَوْنُ}} ({{tr:man firʿawnu}}) is retained as contrast only; local QAC alignment gives {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) as genitive after {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}).

topics.headline: the named ruler feeds the pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the same referent from named source into the emphatic pronoun that opens the diagnosis.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the suffix in {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) as resuming {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}).

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rescue from Pharaoh means rescue from the ruler and the coercive order named by him.
topics.reason: The local word is a foreign proper name, and the CRITICAL rows treat the title-name as gathering both ruler and regime without contradicting the grammar.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this local verdict as part of the Quranic Pharaoh pattern where claimed height becomes classified excess.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete parallels for Pharaoh's claimed highest status (79:24), political elevation (28:4), and height-excess association (10:83).

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) turns the carried rescue-source phrase into explanation: Pharaoh was the one just named, and now the reason he was a source of deliverance must be stated. The particle asserts the diagnosis, while the attached pronoun keeps the referent fixed on Pharaoh before any predicate appears. Because the particle and pronoun are fused in one written bundle, assertion and reference arrive together; the ayah does not pause to rename him. The sound link into {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) helps the explanatory opener flow directly into the state-verb that carries the verdict.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause is not a detached comment; it explains why Pharaoh was the source from which rescue was needed.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) as opening an explanatory clause whose predicate content is {{ar:كَانَ عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:kāna ʿāliyan mina al-musrifīn}}).

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the just-named Pharaoh carried into evaluation by a pronoun rather than by a new named subject.
topics.reason: The attachment cross-reference identifies the third-person suffix in {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) as referring back to {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}).

accusative predicate linked by the deficient verb

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) makes Pharaoh's height a settled state already in force when rescue is narrated. In this frame it is a deficient copula, not a transitive action: it carries the Pharaoh subject and binds him to {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) as predicate. The 3ms perfect form keeps individual accountability on Pharaoh before the plural class widens the verdict. The open a-cadence of the central state phrase gives the verdict breadth before the final class label narrows it. Broader being-language remains relevant only as pressure: the same root-field can mark being by divine command (2:117), while here it records a creaturely condition under judgment; the same surah later uses a similar verdict frame for criminal peoples (44:37).

topics.headline: height is framed as established being
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Pharaoh is judged for an established state of being, not merely for one isolated act.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence parse {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) as a deficient/copular PV.3MS linking the pronoun to {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}).

topics.headline: singular accountability precedes class expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Pharaoh held as an individual bearer of the predicate before the final plural class makes him typological.
topics.reason: The verb is 3ms and matches the Pharaoh pronoun, while the clause later closes on the plural {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}).

topics.headline: being-field pressure stays inside copular judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels arrogance as an occupied status, while local grammar keeps the sense to copular being rather than a broader event of coming-to-be.
topics.reason: The root family supports state and being language, but the local frame signature is copular with no object, so the topic is limited to status-bearing.

topics.headline: common copula becomes a verdict frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ordinary being verb is specialized by verdict contexts, contrasting creaturely judged state here with divine creative command (2:117) and echoing same-surah verdict grammar (44:37).
topics.reason: Because {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) is very common, the intertext is retained as a qualified verdict-frame contrast rather than as a claim that other root branches are locally active.

topics.headline: copula fixes predicate before taxonomy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the syntax from explanation, to fixed predicate, to moral classification.
topics.reason: The clause order is {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:innahu kāna ʿāliyan mina al-musrifīn}}), so classification follows the predicate.

words.gloss_range: accusative active participle predicate meaning high, elevated, or overbearing, locally selected as blameworthy over-positioning
words.root_gloss_range: height, elevation, superiority, loftiness, and overbearing self-positioning; local class phrase selects the blameworthy overreach branch

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: classifying phrase that gives the height its negative moral value

words.prose: {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) supplies the awaited predicate: Pharaoh was high, but the following class phrase tells the reader what kind of height is meant. As an accusative active participle under {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), it characterizes an enduring over-position rather than one moment of rising. The height field can be noble or legitimate elsewhere, but here {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}) selects arrogant, boundary-breaking superiority. The wider height-family pressure, including seeking-superiority language, sharpens the active over-positioning while the local surface remains this participial predicate. That makes the word a pivot between the name and the class: Pharaoh's political elevation (28:4), his claim to highest lordship (79:24), and the height-excess pairing (10:83) are compressed into a settled verdict, while the same-surah warning against being high over God (44:19) returns as Pharaoh's realized posture. Its tanwīn ending also slides into the doubled classifying preposition in {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}), so the move from predicate to classification is heard as joined. Across the boundary, the prior humiliating force meets the tyrant's self-height, and the next ayah's choosing over the worlds (44:32) answers false verticality with a different register of elevation.

topics.headline: participle completes the copular diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is the durable predicate of Pharaoh's state, not a new event of rising.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) as the accusative predicate of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), and QAC tags it as an active participle.

topics.headline: individual predicate before plural class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Pharaoh personally characterized before the definite plural class interprets and generalizes the trait.
topics.reason: The predicate is singular and indefinite, while the following phrase closes with the definite plural {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}).

topics.headline: height becomes blameworthy over-positioning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the vertical image but reads it as arrogant overreach because the final class phrase morally evaluates it.
topics.reason: The root field includes height and superiority, but the local phrase {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}) narrows the active payoff to blameworthy over-positioning.

topics.headline: height-family pressure survives without changing the parse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses active superiority and height-family pressure, while the local surface remains the participial predicate actually present.
topics.reason: The supplied root-family and derivational dispute sharpen the semantic field, but they do not replace the local active participle {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}).

topics.headline: Pharaoh's claimed height is answered as excess
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Pharaoh's vertical politics and highest-lord claim re-read as the settled overbearing height condemned here.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete links to same-surah over-highness (44:19), Pharaoh-height-excess configuration (10:83), highest-lord claim (79:24), and political elevation (28:4).

topics.headline: height mediates between name and class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the ayah's movement from named ruler, through diagnostic height, into transferable moral classification.
topics.reason: The predicate {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) stands between {{ar:فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:firʿawna}}) and the class phrase {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}).

topics.headline: victim-lowering meets tyrant-height
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the regime's downward humiliation and Pharaoh's upward self-positioning as opposite vectors of one oppressive order, then sees 44:32 redirect height into chosen-over language.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link 44:30's humiliating label with {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}), and they point forward to the different vertical register in 44:32.

topics.headline: predicate sound flows into classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the predicate transition into the classifying preposition as a joined movement rather than a detached afterthought.
topics.reason: The observation is anchored in the local transition from {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) to {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}).

words.prose: {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) is the hinge from description to taxonomy. After {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}), it governs {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) as a partitive and classifying phrase, so Pharaoh is counted among a recognized set rather than left as an isolated monster. The repeated particle form frames the ayah's reversal: the first {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) marks rescue away from Pharaoh, while this second {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) inserts Pharaoh among the excessive. Its doubled sound also makes the transition from the nasal predicate ending into the nasal plural closure feel tightly joined.

topics.headline: the second preposition counts Pharaoh inside a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Pharaoh is classified as one member of the excessives, not merely described as high.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) the complement of {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}), classifying the predicate.

topics.reason: The phrase {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}) follows the predicate {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) and closes the ayah.

topics.headline: escape-source becomes moral membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same particle form create an escape-to-classification arc across the ayah.
topics.reason: The opening {{ar:مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:min firʿawna}}) marks removal from Pharaoh, while the closing {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}) classifies Pharaoh.

topics.headline: nasal pressure binds predicate to class

topics.reason: The prosodic rows are anchored in the local transition {{ar:عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan mina al-musrifīn}}).

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) closes the ayah by turning Pharaoh from a singular ruler into one member of a recognized class. The definite plural active participle names people characterized by ongoing overstepping, not one completed mistake, and its genitive position after {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) makes it the class into which Pharaoh is placed. The root range can include waste and immoderation, but after {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) the local force is political and moral overrun beyond rightful bounds. That widens familiar limit-language: consumption excess (7:31) and self-directed excess (39:53) help show the root's range, while Pharaoh's height-excess configuration (10:83) confirms the local association. Ending on this class label makes the verdict transferable: the escaped ruler becomes a diagnostic type of overreaching power. Its crisp final sound also echoes the prior ayah ending (44:30), audibly linking the humiliating punishment there to the class of excessives here.

topics.headline: final word names a recognized class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Pharaoh is not left as a private case; he is placed inside a known plural class.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) as the genitive plural complement of {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}).

topics.headline: participle makes excess a durable identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees excess as an ongoing agentive identity rather than a single passing error.
topics.reason: QAC tags {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) as an active participle noun, and the local plural makes the participial identity group-level.

topics.headline: excess becomes political moral overrun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads the excess class as boundary-breaking power, not merely wasteful spending.
topics.reason: V4 supports overstepping and waste ranges for {{ar:س ر ف}} ({{tr:s-r-f}}), but the local link to {{ar:عَالِيًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿāliyan}}) selects political and moral overrun.

topics.headline: active overstepping image loads the class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the class as people crossing due measure, while the local surface remains the participial plural.
topics.reason: The root family includes overstepping forms, but local activation is constrained to {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) as the active participle plural.

topics.headline: limit language widens into sovereignty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same excess root stretch from consumption and self-directed overrun into Pharaoh's public domination.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete range links to consumption limits (7:31), self-directed excess (39:53), and Pharaoh's height-excess association (10:83).

topics.headline: closing class label generalizes Pharaoh
topics.reader_payoff: The reader leaves the ayah with Pharaoh as a transferable type of overreaching power, not only as an escaped ruler.
topics.reason: The ayah begins with {{ar:مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}} ({{tr:min firʿawna}}) and closes with {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:mina al-musrifīn}}), framing the movement from source to class.

topics.reason: The prosodic rows tie the final {{ar:ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ}} ({{tr:al-musrifīn}}) to its local sound shape and to the prior ayah ending in 44:30.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction “كَانَ عَالِيًا مِنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ” at words 4-7.
baseline_models.mechanism: Temporal predication, domineering height, and boundary excess form one causal profile: Pharaoh occupied a superior position by overpowering, and that position operated through overstepping measure.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence in time makes the elevation an inhabited, temporally predicated state rather than an essence.
Overpowering mastery turns height into an exercised relation over others, not a private feeling.
Crossing a limit supplies the operating rule by which dominating height becomes transgression.

changed_reading.after: He occupied a time-bound dominating height whose exercise consisted in crossing proper bounds.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The pairing of “عَالِيًا” with membership “مِنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ.”
baseline_models.mechanism: High rank becomes epistemically disordered when its holder misplaces things or misses their proper target; excess can therefore be qualitative misdirection, not only too much quantity.

activation_trace.role: Noble or elevated rank supplies the position whose proper use is under question.
Error, heedlessness, and missing the intended placement recast transgression as directional failure.

changed_reading.before: His fault was simply having or spending too much.
changed_reading.after: His elevated position had lost its aim and ordering function: power was placed and directed wrongly.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired prepositions in “مِن فِرْعَوْنَ ... مِنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ.”
baseline_models.mechanism: The first “from” presents a person as an exit-domain or source, while the second places that person inside a class. Pharaoh can thus be read simultaneously as an individual and as a personified domination-system belonging to a repeatable type.

activation_trace.role: Haughty domination gives the personal name enough systemic force to function as a domain one exits.
Limit-crossing defines the wider behavioral class in which the named ruler is only one member.

changed_reading.before: The verse merely identifies the bad ruler from whom someone escaped.
changed_reading.after: Escape is from a ruler-shaped field of domination, while the ruler is demoted from unique monster to one instance of a recurring excessor class.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier prohibition against exalting oneself over or against God, immediately paired with a clear sultan, diagnoses Pharaoh's height as insubordination. Coercive ascent and refusal of compelling evidence remain live together rather than collapsing into generic pride.

activation_trace.role: Mastery anchors the focus description in exercised political force.
The prohibited haughty elevation supplies an explicit relational direction: self-magnification against God.
Compelling proof makes the ascent an epistemic refusal as well as a political act.
Authority and jurisdiction preserve the coexisting reading of rival power rather than proof alone.

structural_cues: 44:19 directly negates exaltation against God and follows it with a clear sultan; 44:31 reuses the elevation root as Pharaoh's diagnosis.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated elevation root and the proof/authority branches. I infer that rising against God converts rank into rejected accountability; alternatively, sultan may be evidentiary without implying rival jurisdiction.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's highness is a broad personality defect.
changed_reading.after: His highness is enacted insubordination: coercive command that also refuses a claim strong enough to answer it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate rescue from humiliating punishment lets the following “from Pharaoh” rename the source-apparatus of that punishment. His height is relational: it keeps others low, so rescue is separation from an imposed vertical order.

activation_trace.role: Dominating mastery supplies the upper pole of the social relation.
Deliverance by separation makes escape from Pharaoh a severing of the relation itself.
Painful punishment identifies what the ruling relation materially administers.
Humiliation through contempt supplies the lowered human position required by tyrannical height.

structural_cues: 44:30 ends with humiliating punishment and 44:31 opens with “from Pharaoh,” creating an immediate appositional or source-specifying hinge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, deliverance, punishment, humiliation, and dominating height. I infer that Pharaoh personifies the preceding punishment-system and that his elevation causes others' abasement; alternatively, the opening phrase may only identify the punishment's agent.

changed_reading.before: An arrogant ruler happened to inflict a humiliating punishment.
changed_reading.after: His very mode of being high was a humiliation-producing apparatus, and deliverance dismantled its relation to the rescued.

context_deltas.mechanism: The abandoned gardens, cultivation, fine station, luxury, and transfer to new heirs materialize highness as an extractive tenure. Repeated past-state language then makes “he was high” sound bounded: the productive landscape persists while its elevated occupants and owners change.

activation_trace.role: Place, position, and rank allow Pharaoh's state to be read as an occupied station.
Abandonment detaches cultivated wealth from those who appeared securely above it.
Cultivation and growth supply the productive substrate beneath elite position.
Softness and luxurious living show how the elevated station was consumed as comfort.
Insolent exuberance connects estate enjoyment to moral overrun rather than neutral prosperity.
Transfer from predecessor to heir proves that possession and rank can outlast one holder and pass to another.
A nearby past-state predication, followed by no reprieve, sharpens the bounded temporal force of the focus copula.

structural_cues: 44:25-28 moves from what was left to productive assets, luxurious enjoyment, and inheritance by another people.
44:29 denies both cosmic mourning and delay immediately before rescue and the focus diagnosis.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the estate-loss sequence, transfer, and repeated past predication. I infer that the estates were the material base of high rank and that transfer exposes rank as tenure; alternatively, the inventory may depict loss without explaining how domination was financed.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's highness is an internal attitude that ended with him.
changed_reading.after: It is a temporary occupancy of productive wealth and social place: an extractive tenure whose assets survive to expose the holder's impermanence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah's choosing upon knowledge and over the worlds creates a non-compromise contrast between two elevations. Pharaoh's is self-produced and limit-breaking; the other is conferred, informed, and therefore measured. Height itself is not condemned uniformly.

activation_trace.role: High rank keeps open a potentially honorable sense that requires contextual discrimination.
Exceeding measure marks what corrupts Pharaoh's elevation rather than making every elevation corrupt.
Selection for good or excellence supplies elevation conferred from outside the chosen group.
Knowledge as disclosed understanding supplies a criterion and measure for the conferred preference.

structural_cues: 44:32 immediately follows with choosing “upon knowledge” and “over the worlds,” repeating the language of vertical relation without repeating Pharaoh's predicate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate juxtaposition, choice, knowledge, and repeated “over/upon” syntax. I infer a criterion distinguishing authorized from self-asserted elevation; alternatively, the sequence may contrast persons without offering a general theory of rank.

changed_reading.before: Being high is itself the offense.
changed_reading.after: The offense is unmeasured, self-authorizing height; context preserves a coexisting form of elevation granted through informed selection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's partitive membership expands through later criminal peoples, universal gathering, and decisive separation. Pharaoh is not an incomparable anomaly but a classified instance of conduct that can recur across peoples and be distinguished in judgment.

activation_trace.role: Limit-crossing defines the portable behavioral criterion of the focus class.
Culpable offense applied to another people extends the focus diagnosis beyond one ruler.
A gathering of groups or mixtures creates the collective field in which types are compared.
Judicial separation of true from false turns broad grouping into accountable classification.

structural_cues: The focus says Pharaoh was “among” excessors; 44:37 compares another criminal people and 44:40 gathers all for a day of separation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies partitive syntax, a second criminal people, gathering, and judgment. I infer a transhistorical behavioral class rather than a unique villain; alternatively, the comparisons may warn by analogy without establishing a formal taxonomy.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh is the singular embodiment of exceptional evil.
changed_reading.after: He is one legible case inside a recurring class, so the focus diagnosis can migrate to any regime that joins elevation to exceeded bounds.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later condemned figure is violently hauled to the center, subjected to force from above at the head, and addressed with titles of might and nobility. This reverses the focus's vertical semantics: claimed mastery becomes forced motion and being mastered from above.

activation_trace.role: The upper direction supplies the focus vector that the later scene reverses.
Violent hauling replaces self-directed ascendancy with coerced movement.
The middle or central place relocates the one who claimed superiority into a punitive center.
Dominance from above makes the former upper position the direction from which subjection arrives.
Leadership and primacy concentrated in the head make the punishment strike the symbolic summit.
The title of overpowering might echoes the mastery claimed by elevated rule.
Nobility and honor preserve the status-title whose force the punitive setting can invert.

structural_cues: 44:47-49 sequences violent hauling, the center of the blaze, pouring from above onto the head, and the address “mighty, noble.”
The surface sound of the hauling verb approaches the focus's elevation language while the packet keeps their roots distinct.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the spatial sequence and status titles. I infer deliberate vertical and titular irony that echoes the focus; alternatively, the condemned figure may be a generic sinner whose pattern resembles Pharaoh without identifying him.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's highness is a static description confined to his historical scene.
changed_reading.after: It installs a reversible vector: the one who masters from above can be driven to the center, struck at his summit, and mastered from above.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a specialized rescue image of flood-safe elevated ground beside literal drowning, but it remains anchored in the focus's height predicate and the sea-rescue sequence. Render it as a spatial analogy that distinguishes kinds of height, not as a claim that the focus word means dry land.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The contrast between Pharaoh being “high” and the immediately preceding rescue.

activation_trace.role: Blameworthy self-elevation supplies the false or socially coercive kind of height.
Flood-safe elevated ground supplies a materially saving height that competes with the ruler's claimed elevation.
Drowning tests which elevation actually preserves life in the surrounding sea scene.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh owns height, while Israel is merely removed from danger.
changed_reading.after: The rescued occupy the only functionally high ground; Pharaoh's social height is exposed as an elevation that cannot save.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it carries a specialized tree-eating creature into political economy, yet it remains rooted in the focus's excessor term and is materially activated by cultivated growth and a later tree. Render it explicitly as an ecological analogy for self-consuming rule, never as the lexical translation of the focus noun.

activation_trace.role: The wood- or leaf-consuming branch turns excess into an internal consumer that damages its own support.
Cultivated growth supplies the productive living substrate consumed by the regime.
A trunked tree reactivates the concrete material domain later in the surah.

changed_reading.before: Excess is an external crossing of a legal or quantitative limit.
changed_reading.after: Excess can also behave like an organism inside a regime's cultivated body, consuming the substrate that keeps its height standing.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it couples the focus root's error-and-missed-target branch to a specialized archery branch under the drowning root. The shared overreach mechanism and sea outcome keep it anchored, but downstream prose must label it a ballistic/material analogy rather than a hidden etymology or narrative event.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins elevated mastery to membership among “ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ.”

activation_trace.role: Missing the intended target makes excess a failure of direction and placement.
Mastery supplies the force that is driven beyond useful measure.
Drawing a bow to its depth supplies the image of force extended toward or beyond its limit.
Drowning supplies the narrative material outcome in which overextended force ends in submergence.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh used an excessive amount of power.
changed_reading.after: His mastery behaves like an overdrawn shot: force passes measure, loses its proper aim, and terminates in the totalizing sea outcome.

strongest_changes: Pharaoh's height became a relational machine that produced the humiliation from which Israel was separated.
The estate-loss sequence changed highness from a personality trait into a temporary, transferable occupancy of productive wealth.
The next ayah preserved a coexisting measured elevation, distinguishing conferred selection from self-authorizing ascent.
The later hauling, center, above, head, and status-title sequence turned static height into a reversible punitive vector.
summary.what_was_special: The focus sustained quantitative excess, qualitative mistargeting, political domination, temporal impermanence, and class membership at once. Material branches then activated flood-safe height, internal tree-consumption, and overdrawn force without requiring those exploratory analogies to replace the stronger readings.
remaining_uncertainties: The opening “from Pharaoh” may appositionally rename the humiliating punishment-system or may only specify its agent.
The condemned figure in 44:47-49 may intentionally echo Pharaoh's vertical profile or may instantiate the same pattern without personal identification.
The high-ground, tree-borer, and overdrawn-bow activations are structurally productive but remain specialized analogies rather than lexical translations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Highness becomes excess when it crosses rightful bounds.** `ع ل و B003` supplies haughty domination and `س ر ف B001` overstepping the limit. The apposition identifies the source of humiliating punishment, then explains his height by classing him among transgressors; I infer that domination is elevation maintained beyond jurisdiction. The ayah reads `عاليًا` as structurally excessive, not genuinely noble.
2. **The earlier prohibition is historically instantiated.** `ع ل و B004` supplies mastery. Pharaoh's mastery answers “do not exalt yourselves over God” in 44:19; I infer that control of God's servants is the concrete form of that attempted mastery. The ayah retrospectively gives the prohibition a political body.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 44:48 pours punishment from above onto the head, and 44:49 dismantles claimed might and nobility. That vertical reversal makes Pharaoh's `عاليًا` an early instance of a status grammar the judgment scene later overturns bodily.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Pharaoh’s height is enacted domination.** `ع ل و` `B003` is haughty domination and `B004` gaining mastery; `س ر ف` `B001` is overstepping a proper limit. He is named as the source from whom the group was rescued out of humiliating torment (`44:30`), after a noble station has lost its holders (`44:26-29`) and before the rescued are knowingly selected (`44:32`). Height therefore functions as status maintained by degrading others, not neutral rank. The packet supplies humiliation, removal, and comparative selection; I infer **domination past limit -> unstable elevation**.

2. **Excess internally bores through the productive order.** `س ر ف` `B004` is the wood-eating insect that bores trees, while this ayah’s window still contains crops, a fertile noble station, and ease (`44:26-27`). The material branch makes excess analogous to an internal consumer of the very system that supports height. The packet supplies vegetation and the accepted insect image; I infer **unchecked domination -> internal erosion of its resource base**. This is exploratory, but it gives `ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ` a coherent ecological mechanism rather than treating excess as quantity alone.

3. **The apparently high state is exposed as bad condition.** `ك و ن` `B001` predicates a state, while `B006` admits a bad state or condition. Within five later ayat, the rescued group is knowingly chosen and given signs (`44:32-33`), whereas the current speaker-group denies renewed life (`44:34-36`). That juxtaposition assigns Pharaoh’s high state the role of a negative model: elevation without knowledge mislocates value. The packet supplies the comparative succession; I infer **misranked height -> epistemic and political failure**. `كَانَ عَالِيًا` acquires an adverse retrospective frame.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The captive figure’s ironic `ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ` in `44:49` exposes another unsupported claim to rank, while `ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ` in `44:57` relocates true greatness to escape plus bounty. Pharaoh’s height retrospectively becomes mismeasured elevation, not greatness itself.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini çekirdek kabul eder ve buna olma adları ile geçmiş ya da şimdiki bildirme kullanımlarını bağlar. Pekiştirme, ayırma ve ettirgen oluşturma kullanımları aynı dal içinde bağımlı kullanımlar olarak durur; yer, konum ve üstlenme dalları bu çekirdeğin yerine geçirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bu dal, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini ve bu olmanın geçmiş ya da şimdiki anda bildirilmesini anlatır. Olma adları, pekiştirme ya da ayırma işlevli bağlı sözler ve bir şeyi oldurup oluşmasını sağlama buna bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin gerçekleşmesi, ortaya çıkması ve bulunur halde olması çekirdektir.
Olma ve oluş adları bu çekirdeğin adlaştırılmış biçimleridir.
Geçmişteki bir durumun haber verilmesi veya şimdiki olmanın bildirilmesi bu alana bağlıdır.
Pekiştirme ve gelen kişiyi kapsam dışı bırakma gibi bağlı söz dizimleri çekirdeğe ek kullanımlardır.
Bir şeyi oldurmak, onun gerçekleşmesini sağlama yönünde ettirgen bir uzantıdır.

Deve ve dişi deve örneklerinde irilik, uzunluk ve sağlam yaratılış birlikte belirir.
Kişi ve hayvan uygulamalarında kapsam farkları bulunur, fakat hepsi bedensel yapı alanında kalır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kanıt, uzunluk ve irilik anlamını insan ve deve örnekleriyle verir. Kimi kullanımda cinsiyet veya tür sınırı tartışmalı görünse de dalın ortak çekirdeği bedensel uzunluk, irilik ve sağlam yapıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Uzunluk, irilik ve bedensel yapı sınırını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir yandan lohusa kadının temizlenip kurtulmasını özellikle sınırlar, diğer yandan hastalıktan kurtulan erkek için de bir yapı verir. Dal korunabilir, fakat tanım bu iki bağlı yapıyla sınırlanmalı ve genel yükselme ya da her türlü iyileşme anlamına genişletilmemelidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam kolokasyondur; tanım yalnız lohusalık ve hastalık yapılarındaki kurtulma değerini verir.

concept_map.definition: Sınırlı yapılarda, lohusa kadının temizlenip esenliğe çıkması veya erkeğin hastalıktan kurtulmasıdır; genel yükselme değil, sıkıntılı bedensel halden çıkıştır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, bedensel sıkıntı halinden kurtulup esenliğe çıkmadır.
Lohusa kadının temizlenmesi ve kurtulması en belirgin sınırlı kullanımdır.
Hastalıktan kurtulan erkek örneği de verilir, fakat bu dal genel iyileşme anlamına genişletilmez.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kanıt, lohusalıktan temizlenme ve hastalıktan kurtulma yapılarını aynı sınırlı kurtulma alanında verir. Kanıt içinde kullanım sınırı dar tutulduğu için tanım genel iyileşme veya genel yükselme anlamına açılmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalı fiil anlamından ayrı olarak ilgeç, adlaşmış görev sözü ve kalıplaşmış emir kullanımlarıyla verir. Geçici çerçeve bunu şeref veya somut yükselme anlamına taşımadığı için kaynakla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, dil bilgisi görevi ve kalıplaşmış söz kullanımıdır; yükselme fiili değildir.

concept_map.definition: Bağımsız yükselme fiili değil, belirli dil bilgisi görevlerinde kullanılan ilgeç, adlaşmış biçim veya kalıplaşmış emir sözüdür; bağlama göre üzerinde, yanından, al ya da ver değerleri taşır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, fiilden ayrı bir görev sözü ve ilgeç kullanımıdır.
Kimi yapılarda üzerinde, yanından veya üstünden gibi adlaşmış yön değerleri oluşur.
Kalıplaşmış emir yapılarında al veya bana ver gibi yöneltilmiş görev değerleri bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kanıt, dalı ilgeç ve adlaşmış/kalıplaşmış görev sözü olarak verir. Bazı örnekler konum veya kaynak yönünü, bazıları ise al ve ver gibi emir değerini gösterir; bunlar yükselme fiiliyle karıştırılmamalıdır.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök ailesi yukarı ve yüksek konum çekirdeğinden fiziksel yükselme, üst taraf, saygın mevki, kınanan üstünlük taslama, yapı içinde baskın gelme ve sözlükselleşmiş ad/ilgeç kullanımlarına yayılan çok dallı bir ağdır. Bazı dallar çıplak yükseklikten, bazıları yalnız belirli kalıp veya yerleşmiş addan okunmalıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi, anlamın çekirdeğini bir işte belirlenmiş sınırı veya uygun ölçüyü aşmak olarak verir. Harcamada savurganlık, suyu yararsız yere tüketme, yemede ölçüyü kaçırma ve öldürmede hakkın ötesine geçme bu genel çekirdeğin bağlama bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel sınır aşma çekirdeğini korur; harcama, yeme, su ve öldürme anlamlarını yalnızca kendi yapıları içinde uzmanlaşmış kullanımlar olarak ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Bir işte belirlenmiş sınırı, uygun miktarı veya gözetilmesi gereken amacı aşarak ölçüsüz davranmaktır. Harcama, yeme, su kullanımı ve öldürme alanlarında bu aşma, şeyi hakkı ya da yararı dışında kullanma biçimini alabilir.

facets.statement: Bir eylemde belirlenmiş sınırı veya uygun ölçüyü aşma ve ölçülü tutumun karşısına geçme.
Para, yiyecek veya suyu uygun yer, miktar ya da yararın dışında kullanarak boşa harcama.
Öldürmede faille sınırlı kalmayıp başka birine yönelerek hak sınırını aşma.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, her eylemde ölçü veya hak sınırını aşmayı çekirdek sayar. Bu çekirdek harcamada savurganlık, suyun yararsız yere gitmesi, yemede uygun ölçünün aşılması ve öldürmede hakkın ötesine geçilmesiyle somutlaşır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Genel çekirdeği karşılar; belirli kullanım alanlarında aşılmış olan sınır ayrıca belirtilmelidir.

error_profile.preserves: Sınırın ve uygun ölçünün geçilmesi yönünü eksiksiz korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi amaçlanandan başka türlü yapmak, hedeflenen şeye isabet edememek veya onu gözden kaçırmaktır. Bazı kullanımlarda bu çekirdek, bir şeyi bilmemeyi, tanıyamamayı ya da belirsiz bulmayı anlatır.

facets.statement: Amaçlanan şeye isabet edemeyerek yanılma veya bir şeyi uygun olmayan yere koyma.
Bir kişiyi veya şeyi fark etmeyip gözden kaçırma ve ona gereken dikkati göstermeme.
Bir şeyi bilmeme, tanıyamama veya görünüşü belirsiz kaldığı için ayırt edememe.
